# Northvale has frozen your money. We’re angry too.

**By Inês, Product Designer at Pinha**  
**Tuesday, 10 November 2026**

On Friday morning, without warning, Northvale Payments blocked every outgoing transfer from Pinha.

Since then, you have not been able to withdraw your own money.

I’ve spent the last few days trying to work out how to write this without hiding behind careful, empty language. I don’t want to give you a polished corporate apology. I don’t want to ask for your patience as though patience is the reasonable response to being locked out of your savings.

You have every right to be furious. We are furious too.

I’m angry with Northvale for doing this. I’m also angry with us for putting ourselves—and therefore you—in a position where one partner could switch off access like this.

So here is what we know, what we are doing, and what you can do now. No reassuring fog, and no date we cannot honestly promise.

## What happened

Northvale Payments is the electronic money institution, based in Vilnius, that holds Pinha customers’ money. It keeps those funds in safeguarded accounts, separate from Northvale’s own money.

On **Wednesday, 4 November**, Northvale emailed us to say it was commercially terminating our relationship, giving **30 days’ notice**. The only explanation offered was a “risk appetite review”. No specific incident was identified, and we were not given a meaningful reason for the decision.

Then, at **09:00 on Friday, 6 November**, Northvale blocked all outgoing transfers. It did this without warning and before its own 30-day notice period had ended. Deposits and round-ups stopped as well.

Our Northvale account manager stopped answering our calls on Friday. When we call, we get a voicemail in Lithuanian.

A 30-day notice period should mean 30 days. Freezing people’s savings two days later, with no warning, is not some abstract “risk” decision to us. It is cowardice, and the people paying for it are you.

## Your money has not disappeared

This is the most important thing I can tell you: **the money is safeguarded. It is not lost.**

Northvale holds customer funds separately from its own money and cannot use those funds for its own purposes. This is not Northvale’s money to spend.

But I need to be just as clear about the part that is causing so much harm: **safeguarded is not the same as accessible right now.** Northvale is preventing withdrawals, and we cannot move the money to another provider until Northvale releases the funds and provides what is needed for the transfer.

I know that distinction may feel infuriatingly technical when you are the one staring at a balance you cannot touch. If someone tells you your money is safe but you cannot pay your rent with it, that does not solve your problem today.

We understand that. We are not treating “the money is safeguarded” as the end of the conversation.

## We made a serious mistake too

Pinha was built around a simple idea: rounding up everyday purchases should make saving feel possible, even when putting money aside feels difficult.

I designed the screen that says: **“Your money is always yours. Take it out any time.”**

I look at that sentence now and feel sick.

Not because the money belongs to anyone else—it doesn’t—but because, at this moment, you cannot take it out. We wrote a promise about access while relying on a single payments partner to make that access possible. Northvale’s actions are Northvale’s responsibility. Having only one partner and no working backup was ours.

We were naïve. We trusted the structure we had put in place, and we did not build enough protection against the partner controlling it failing us.

That was our mistake, and we are not going to make you read between the lines to find us admitting it.

You can be angry with Northvale. You can be angry with us too. I am not going to tell you to calm down.

## What we are doing

I have signed an agreement with a new partner, **Ostra Bank in Lisbon**.

That is real progress, but it does not mean we can flip a switch tomorrow. Completing the migration requires two things outside our sole control:

1. Northvale must send the balances file and release the customer funds.
2. Banco de Portugal must give the necessary approval for the migration.

Our current working estimate is **10 to 15 working days**, but **this is an estimate, not a deadline and not a promise**. It depends on Northvale cooperating and on the regulatory process. I will not turn an estimate into a date just because a date would make this post sound more reassuring.

We also filed formal complaints on **Saturday, 7 November**, with **Banco de Portugal** and the **Lithuanian central bank**.

Rui, our CEO, is spending today in calls with lawyers and Banco de Portugal. The rest of our small team is working on the migration, pressing Northvale for releases, and answering your messages.

We are pursuing every route available to us. When something concrete changes, we will tell you.

## If your situation is urgent

Some of you are not waiting for savings you had put aside for someday. You need this money now.

One person in Porto wrote to us in capital letters. She has spent three years saving for a deposit on a car, and the dealership has given her until **Friday, 13 November**. I read her message on the metro and nearly cried.

I cannot pretend that a complaint process or a migration estimate answers what she is facing.

If you are at risk of being unable to pay rent, covering essential medical costs, or dealing with another immediate crisis such as losing your job, please email:

**urgent@pinha.example**

Use the subject line:

**URGENTE**

Tell us briefly what is happening and include any relevant deadline. We are using these cases to press for **individual releases from Northvale**. I have to be honest: Northvale has not agreed to release these payments, so writing to this address does not guarantee that we can get your money out. But we are trying case by case, and we want the most urgent situations in front of us rather than buried in a general support queue.

For other support questions, our normal channels remain open. Since Friday, we have received around **1,900 support emails**. Three people are answering them, and the current reply time is approximately **two days**. We know that is slow when you are worried about your money, and we are working through the messages.

We have also **cancelled the monthly Pinha fee for November and December for everyone**. You do not need to request this.

## What happens next

We will publish updates on this blog **every Monday and Thursday until this is resolved**. We will use those updates to tell you what has moved, what has not, and what we are still waiting for—including when the answer is that Northvale has not cooperated.

Right now, the practical steps are:

- **If your situation is urgent**, email **urgent@pinha.example** with the subject **URGENTE**.
- **For other questions**, contact support, knowing that replies are currently taking around two days.
- **Check this blog on Mondays and Thursdays** for verified updates.
- **Do not expect the 10-to-15-working-day estimate to be a guaranteed release date.** We will confirm timing only when we can stand behind it.

There is no version of this post that makes the situation acceptable. People planned around money they had every reason to believe they could withdraw. Some of those plans are now at risk. A safeguards explanation does not pay a deposit, cover a prescription, or keep someone housed.

What we can do is be direct with you, fight for the releases, complete the migration, and stop pretending that everything is fine simply because the balances still exist.

Your money is yours. Right now, you are being prevented from reaching it. We will not treat that as a minor operational issue, and we will not go quiet while we work to fix it.

**Inês**
